column1: # bin/lib/reachability-exemptions.tsv — the ONLY licence for a bin/ executable that no
# live entry point can reach. Read by bin/lib/reachability.sh; enforced by
# test/bin-reachability-gate.test.sh; reported by bin/heimdall-deadcode.
# FORMAT (tab-separated, three columns, one row per name):
#     name <TAB> recheck-by (YYYY-MM-DD) <TAB> reason
# WHY EVERY ROW EXPIRES. An exemption that never expires is a second way to go quietly
# dead. Someone writes "standalone by design" once, nobody looks again, and the binary
# rots under cover of its own excuse — which is exactly how bin/heimdall-brief would
# have survived even WITH a reachability gate. So the date is not decoration: past it,
# the gate FAILS until a human wires the tool up, deletes it, or re-justifies it with a
# new date. Four rot conditions are enforced against this file, not one:
#     MALFORMED  no name, no reason, or a recheck date that is not a real ISO date
#     EXPIRED    past its recheck date
#     STALE      the name is reachable again, so the exclusion is now hiding nothing
#     ORPHAN     bin/<name> no longer exists, and a leftover row would silently
#                pre-clear a future executable that reuses the name
# THIS FILE IS NOT A REFERENCE SURFACE. It names every exempt executable, so if the
# scanner read it, writing an exemption would MAKE the binary look reachable and the
# escape hatch would become the defect. reach_build() excludes it from the node set and
# the scan set; test/bin-reachability-gate.test.sh §3c proves the exclusion holds.
# RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-08. The gate previously carried its own flat "does any file name
# it?" matcher and reported the nine BY DESIGN / KNOWN GAP names below as "now wired —
# remove these rows". They are not wired. Every one of them was re-checked against a
# live entry point and every one is still unreachable; the flat matcher was reading
# mentions from other dead files as proof of life. The rows stay. If you meet that
# "stale, remove them" claim again, re-run `heimdall-deadcode --why <name>` before
# deleting anything — a row removed on a false staleness report silently converts an
# acknowledged dead tool into an unacknowledged one.
# THREE HONEST CATEGORIES. Only the first is a compliment.
#     BY DESIGN   no runtime caller is possible or wanted — a human runs it directly.
#     KNOWN GAP   it SHOULD be wired and is not. Recorded rather than hidden.
#     DEAD        unreachable, found by the 2026-08-08 transitive-liveness audit and
#                 not yet triaged. Recorded so the ratchet can hold against NEW dead
#                 code while these are decided. Short recheck window on purpose.

column1: # ── DEAD — the 2026-08-08 transitive-liveness finding, awaiting triage ───────────
# Each of these passed the OLD flat "something mentions it" rule and fails the transitive
# one. In every case the only mouths naming them are themselves unreachable: their own
# implementation library, a sibling that is equally dead, or each other.
# ALL ELEVEN triaged 2026-09-08 on their FIRST recheck-by expiry (2026-09-07) — the
# mechanism did its job (56 passed/0 failed -> 54 passed/22 failed, exactly 11 x the
# two failure-instances this file's own header documents) and forced a real re-triage
# instead of a blanket renewal. Each was checked via `heimdall-deadcode --why <name>`
# (never assumed from a passing test alone — see this file's own re-verify-before-
# deleting note above) plus a full, unstubbed run of its dedicated test suite:
#   WIRED — a real dispatcher arm now lives in bin/heimdall, so the row here is
#   removed (an exemption row for a now-reachable name is itself STALE per this
#   file's own rot rule): heimdall-branch-context, heimdall-collision, heimdall-task,
#   heimdall-land, heimdall-issue-corpus, heimdall-memory, heimdall-vm-bench.
#   RECLASSIFIED to BY DESIGN above — genuinely human/operator-run, not dead (see
#   each row there for why): heimdall-cost-model-refresh, heimdall-cost-report,
#   heimdall-s6-manifest, heimdall-s6-sweep.
# Nothing in this batch was actually dead code — every one was real, tested, wanted
# capability missing only its wiring or its category. This section stays empty as
# the historical record of that audit; the next transitive-liveness finding starts
# a new dated section below it, it does not reuse this one.
# ── DEAD — the 2026-08-22 comment-stripping + dispatcher-hop-ceiling audit ───────
# Found after bin/lib/reachability.sh stopped counting comment-only mentions as
# invocation edges and stopped crediting bin/heimdall's dispatch table with LIVE
# status for hops it merely selects at runtime. heimdall-spawn was a
# two-corpse chain: its only real (non-comment) caller, heimdall-watch, was itself
# unreachable (a KNOWN GAP rather than DEAD because ITS OWN header named a concrete
# integration plan); the chain's tail had none of its own.
# heimdall-queue was a second instance of the same shape, listed here alongside
# heimdall-spawn, until 2026-08-23: the `hmd queue` dispatcher arm gave
# bin/heimdall a real, non-comment exec path into both it and bin/heimdall-drain
# (verified via `heimdall-deadcode --why heimdall-queue` / `--why heimdall-drain`
# before deleting, per this file's own re-verify-before-deleting rule above, not
# assumed from the commit message alone). That row, heimdall-drain's KNOWN GAP row
# above, and the two heimdall-issue-* KNOWN GAP rows above (independently made
# REACHABLE the same day via the new commands/maintain-check.md) are gone.
# TRIAGED 2026-11-12, on this chain's second recheck-by expiry (heimdall-spawn
# 2026-10-23, heimdall-watch 2026-11-08) — operator decision: wire or delete, never
# re-date. DELETED, both: heimdall-watch's whole body is a loop that hands each
# sentinel to heimdall-spawn (it exits 2 at startup without it), it had no test and
# no trigger, and the pre-push hook its own header asked for never landed in three
# months; heimdall-spawn had no other caller. Gone with them: sentinels/lib/brief.sh
# (the brief hydrator only spawn sourced — bin/heimdall-brief over bin/lib/brief-core.sh
# is the one assembler now) and the spawn cases of test/brief-fail-closed.test.sh.
# Kept: the standalone sentinels/*.sh scripts, each with its own CLI and report path.
# Checked with `heimdall-deadcode --why` first, per this file's re-verify rule above.
# ── DEAD — the 2026-08-28 python-docstring-stripping audit ──────────────────────
# Found after bin/lib/reachability.sh learned to stop tokenizing the CONTENT of a
# Python triple-quoted docstring as code when it opens as a bare expression
# statement (a module or function docstring that merely prose-names another tool
# no longer creates an edge to it; a triple-quoted string assigned to a variable
# or passed as an argument still does, since a real invocation can legitimately
# live inside one of those — see bin/lib/reachability.sh's reach_extract_tokens
# header comment for the exact rule).
# TRIAGED 2026-10-01, on this section's first recheck-by expiry (2026-09-27) — the mechanism
# did its job: bin-reachability-gate failed both of its per-row instances (SHIPPED BUT
# UNREACHABLE + EXEMPTION ROT) and forced a real triage instead of a blanket renewal.
# heimdall-529-scan was checked with `heimdall-deadcode --why heimdall-529-scan` (DEAD: every
# mention outside its own test was a comment or docstring), a full-tree grep, and its own full
# test suite, then:
#   WIRED — a real `529-scan)` dispatcher arm now lives in bin/heimdall, so the row here is
#   removed (a row for a now-reachable name is itself STALE per this file's own rot rule).
#   Not deleted: it is real, tested capability that bin/lib/pressure_control.py,
#   bin/heimdall-agent-resume, hooks/heimdall-429-detect.sh and bin/heimdall-session-usage all
#   cite as the reference overload classifier, and install.sh puts only hmd/heimdall on PATH,
#   so without an arm no installed operator could run it. Not renewed: nothing names a plan to
#   wire it — the only statement of the intent is the follow-up note in
#   docs/analysis/2026-08-25-transcript-529-detection.md, with no branch, plan or commit
#   behind it in the five weeks since.
#   NOT DONE, ON PURPOSE: a feed from its output into `heimdall-pressure record`. Its own
#   header leaves that "to a future caller", `record` is not idempotent (a re-scan would
#   manufacture a threshold breach out of one real event), and it changes spawn concurrency —
#   an owner's call, not a side effect of clearing a reachability gate.
#   heimdall-face-test, the other bin this audit un-hid, is under BY DESIGN above.
# This section is now empty as the historical record of that audit; the next finding starts
# a new dated section below it, it does not reuse this one.
